liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): The jam sequence is described as very effective and on point throughout the performance; The jam moves to interesting places, making more sense than in many other 1974 shows [9][13]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): The transition from the Playing In The Band jam into Wharf Rat is described as sweet [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.motb0056.88979.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1974-07-21.sony22p.bertrando-miller.88553.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 183 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [2]
- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.89033.flac24**: source not stated; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [3]
- **gd74-07-21.fob-patched.miller.31436.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4.3/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Vocals are drowned out in most of the show, though the second set sounds slightly better; Sound is cleaner than the other source, with Phil's vocals heard much more clearly [14][15]
- **gd74-07-21.bertrando.weiner.8241.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 171 min; rated 4.5/5 by 14 [5]. Said about its sound: Clear bass and minimal crowd noise, noted as a high-quality pre-digital audience recording; Vocals are somewhat clear, but the crowd quiets down significantly when the jams begin; Captures the Wall of Sound vibe, which the reviewer claims soundboards cannot replicate [8][10][12]

## Around the show

- Summer atmosphere at the Hollywood Bowl in 1974 creates a vivid, mouth-watering experience [9]
- Taper banter includes a question about a roach clip, though it is not distracting [10]
- Routine 1974 performance, less groundbreaking than June 26, August 4, or August 6 shows [7]
- Not in the vault, making this audience recording the only available source for this date [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.motb0056.88979.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Adam Egert; source: 2 x Sony ECM-22P => Sony TC-152SD >> MAC >> Sony TC-D5M => TEAC AN-300 [Dolby Encode] => Technics RS-1506US [3.75 IPS] [1]
- **gd1974-07-21.sony22p.bertrando-miller.88553.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-22P -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat DAround [2]. Also: Rob Bertrando lent his cassette master, which was copied to cassette twice before transfer; Scarlet Begonias end and Playin' In The Band teases are patched from unknown mics [2]
- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.89033.flac24**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Adam Egert; source: FOB Cassette (MAC) Analog Copy Instances: Reel 1 (R1) Medium Stock Brands: MAC = Sony C90 [CrO2], R1 = Maxell UD 35-90 2 x Sony ECM-22P => Sony TC-152SD >> MAC… [3]. Also: Setlist details confirm specific song transitions, including Mississippi Half-Step into It Must Have Been The Roses [3]
- **gd74-07-21.fob-patched.miller.31436.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Rob Bertrando and Ed Friedman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Ken Stuart; source: Audience: Sony ECM-22P [4]. Also: Text file indicates this is an entirely new transfer, in addition to being patched; Scarlet Begonias end and part of Truckin' patched from unknown mics via cassette master [4][15]
- **gd74-07-21.bertrando.weiner.8241.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-22P mics [5]. Also: Charlie Miller patched this source with a previously uncirculated one to create a complete show; Rob Bertrando used Sony ECM-22P mics and a Sony TC-152 cassette master for the recording; Noah Weiner seeded the recording to etree after an AudMC, Reel, DAT, and CD chain [5][11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.gratefulseconds.com: [The Wall Comes to the Hollywood Bowl, July 21, 1974](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2017/03/the-wall-comes-to-hollywood-bowl-july.html) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/hollywood-bowl) [21]
